## 7. Variants: The Product Family Model
The system must distinguish the product style from the sellable variant.
A common apparel family is one style with multiple colors and sizes.
Column: Level
Column: Example
Column: Rule
Product family variant level: Parent / style
Parent / style example: TSHIRT-001
Parent / style rule: Represents the underlying product/style.
Product family variant level: Color child
Color child example: TSHIRT-001-BLK
Color child rule: One color variation.
Product family variant level: Size child
Size child example: TSHIRT-001-BLK-M
Size child rule: One sellable size/color combination.
Product family variant level: Marketplace listing
Marketplace listing example: Marketplace-specific SKU/listing ID
Marketplace listing rule: External representation of the sellable item.
### Core Variation Invariants
Store a complete size × color matrix.
The stored size × color matrix includes unavailable combinations.
Never silently create a variant that the seller did not provide.
Keep seller SKU stable even if marketplace identifiers differ.
Record parent-child relationships separately from marketplace-specific variation rules.
Amazon's listing schema explicitly distinguishes parent and child listing levels.
In Amazon's listing schema, different attributes are applicable to parent and child listing levels.

### 11.1 Source-of-Truth Priority
Source-of-Truth Priority item 20 (first listed): Seller-provided structured data.
Source-of-Truth Priority item 21 (second): Seller-provided documents/labels/size charts.
Source-of-Truth Priority item 21 (second): authoritative product assets.
Source-of-Truth Priority item 22 (third): Connected catalog/PIM/ERP data.
Connected catalog/PIM/ERP data is used only if explicitly connected and trusted.
Source-of-Truth Priority item 23 (fourth): Existing marketplace data.
Existing marketplace data is used when it is the seller's own authoritative listing data.
Source-of-Truth Priority item 24 (fifth): Derived values from deterministic normalization or category rules.
Source-of-Truth Priority item 25 (sixth): AI-generated inference.
AI-generated inference only when the field is non-critical.
AI-generated inference only when the inference is clearly permitted.
Never use an AI guess to fill a critical factual/compliance field.
## 12. Step-by-Step Autonomous Listing Workflow
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 1: UNDERSTAND PRODUCT
STEP 1 goal: Build a complete understanding of the product before generating a marketplace listing.
STEP 1 input: Seller form
STEP 1 input: spreadsheet
STEP 1 input: images
STEP 1 input: website/catalog data
STEP 1 input: size chart
STEP 1 input: product documents
STEP 1 input: connected systems
STEP 1 action: Identify product and variants
STEP 1 action: separate facts from marketing language
STEP 1 action: detect missing data
STEP 1 action: detect conflicting data
STEP 1 action: detect duplicate data
STEP 1 action: determine reliable vs confirmation-needed facts
STEP 1 output: Structured product facts.
STEP 1 output: each product fact carries its source.
STEP 1 output: each product fact carries its confidence.
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 2: CLASSIFY
STEP 2 goal: Decide the correct product category and sub-category for each marketplace.
STEP 2 action: Identify product type (T-shirt, shirt, dress, jeans, etc.)
STEP 2 action: identify audience/gender
STEP 2 action: map canonical product to marketplace taxonomy
STEP 2 action: verify seller category eligibility
STEP 2 action: use evidence & rules (no random guesses)
STEP 2 output: Canonical category
STEP 2 output: marketplace-specific category/product type
STEP 2 output: confidence
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 3: EXTRACT ATTRIBUTES
STEP 3 goal: Populate all product attributes from the available evidence.
STEP 3 action: Extract color
STEP 3 action: Extract size
STEP 3 action: Extract fabric
STEP 3 action: Extract fit
STEP 3 action: Extract pattern
STEP 3 action: Extract neckline
STEP 3 action: Extract sleeve
STEP 3 action: Extract length
STEP 3 action: Extract closure
STEP 3 action: Extract occasion
STEP 3 action: normalize synonyms into controlled values
STEP 3 action: preserve original seller value
STEP 3 action: preserve normalized value
STEP 3 action: track source
STEP 3 action: detect contradictions (e.g., '100% cotton' vs 'cotton-poly blend')
STEP 3 output: Complete canonical attribute set.
STEP 3 output: missing/conflicting fields identified.
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 4: FILL MARKETPLACE SCHEMA
STEP 4 goal: Transform the canonical product into the exact field structure expected by each selected marketplace.
STEP 4 action: Load current marketplace/category schema
STEP 4 action: map canonical fields to portal fields
STEP 4 action: apply allowed-value enums
STEP 4 action: mark required fields
STEP 4 action: mark conditional fields
STEP 4 action: mark optional fields
STEP 4 action: mark unsupported fields
STEP 4 action: build parent/child variation structure
STEP 4 action: map media roles
STEP 4 action: map content fields
STEP 4 output: Marketplace-ready draft for each marketplace.
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 5: GENERATE CONTENT
STEP 5 goal: Create customer-facing listing content from verified product facts.
STEP 5 creates: Title
STEP 5 creates: bullets/key features
STEP 5 creates: description
STEP 5 creates: search keywords
STEP 5 creates: size/fit copy
STEP 5 creates: portal-specific content fields
STEP 5 rule: No unsupported claims
STEP 5 rule: no invented specs
STEP 5 rule: do not copy prohibited content
STEP 5 rule: keep consistent factual identity
STEP 5 rule: adapt tone/format to marketplace rules
STEP 5 output: Content package with source traceability.
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 6: VALIDATE
STEP 6 goal: Catch problems before marketplace submission.
STEP 6 validate checklist: Required fields present
STEP 6 validate checklist: allowed values
STEP 6 validate checklist: parent/child relationship valid
STEP 6 validate checklist: color & size consistency
STEP 6 validate checklist: image presence
STEP 6 validate checklist: image association
STEP 6 validate checklist: price/MRP consistency
STEP 6 validate checklist: product identifier rules
STEP 6 validate checklist: HSN/tax fields
STEP 6 validate checklist: country of origin
STEP 6 validate checklist: manufacturer details
STEP 6 validate checklist: content policy checks
STEP 6 validate checklist: no conflicting facts
STEP 6 output value: `PASS`
STEP 6 output value: `BLOCKED`
STEP 6 output value: `NEEDS HUMAN INPUT`
STEP 6 output is given with field-level reasons.
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 7: FIND MISSING DATA
STEP 7 goal: Determine whether missing information can be recovered automatically.
STEP 7: Try recovery sources in this strict hierarchy.
STEP 7 hierarchy 1: Existing canonical product record.
STEP 7 hierarchy 2: Same brand's trusted catalog conventions.
STEP 7 hierarchy 3: Connected PIM/ERP/catalog.
STEP 7 hierarchy 4: Existing marketplace listing owned by the seller.
STEP 7 hierarchy 5: Seller-provided files/assets.
STEP 7 hierarchy 6: Deterministic category mapping.
STEP 7 hierarchy 7: Ask seller.
STEP 7 output: Missing fields reduced to the smallest set genuinely required.
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 8: ASK HUMAN ONLY WHEN NECESSARY
STEP 8 goal: Ask the seller one clear question instead of sending them back to a large form.
STEP 8 example question: 'What is the fabric composition: 100% cotton or 95% cotton / 5% elastane?'
STEP 8 example question: 'Please provide the size chart for this product.'
STEP 8 example question: 'Which MRP should be used for the black variant?'
STEP 8 example question: 'Please confirm whether this is a women's or unisex product.'
STEP 8 question must include: Why information is required
STEP 8 question must include: which products/variants it affects
STEP 8 question must include: exact expected answer
STEP 8 question must include: optional safe suggestions
STEP 8 post-response: Update canonical record
STEP 8 post-response: resume automatically from blocked step
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 9: SUBMIT
STEP 9 goal: Send the validated listing to the selected marketplace(s).
STEP 9 action: Submit only required and permitted fields
STEP 9 action: record submission time
STEP 9 action: record job ID/reference
STEP 9 action: store exact version submitted
STEP 9 action: update status from Draft/Ready to Submitted/Pending
STEP 9 output: Marketplace submission record.
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 10: CHECK STATUS
STEP 10 goal: Determine what happened after submission.
STEP 10 possible outcome: Accepted/processing
STEP 10 possible outcome: Active/live
STEP 10 possible outcome: Rejected
STEP 10 possible outcome: Partially accepted
STEP 10 possible outcome: Missing information
STEP 10 possible outcome: Validation failure
STEP 10 possible outcome: Pending marketplace review
STEP 10 possible outcome: Account/category permission issue
STEP 10 rule: Keep checking until a terminal state is reached.
STEP 10 rule: Keep checking until a human action is required (alternative stop condition).
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 11: FIX ERRORS
STEP 11 goal: Diagnose errors.
STEP 11 goal: Resolve errors.
STEP 11 goal: errors are resolved without making the seller repeat the process.
STEP 11 for every error: Capture error code
STEP 11 for every error: Capture error message
STEP 11 for every error: identify affected SKU
STEP 11 for every error: identify affected field
STEP 11 for every error: translate to plain language
STEP 11 for every error: determine if auto-fixable
STEP 11 for every error: apply deterministic fix
STEP 11 for every error: revalidate
STEP 11 auto-fixable class: Wrong portal enum mapped from known canonical value
STEP 11 auto-fixable class: formatting issue
STEP 11 auto-fixable class: safely calculable derived field
STEP 11 auto-fixable class: incorrect parent/child mapping
STEP 11 human-required class: Missing factual product info
STEP 11 human-required class: conflicting seller data
STEP 11 human-required class: brand authorization/approval
STEP 11 human-required class: account issue
STEP 11 human-required class: compliance evidence request
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 12: RESUBMIT
STEP 12 goal: Send the corrected listing back to the marketplace.
STEP 12 action: Keep same seller SKU/identity
STEP 12 action: record correction made
STEP 12 action: increment submission attempt count
STEP 12 action: submit only after validation passes
STEP 12 action: preserve failed versions for audit
Autonomous listing workflow STEP 13: CONFIRM LIVE
STEP 13 goal: Confirm the product is genuinely sellable/live.
STEP 13 minimum confirmation: Status = live/active
STEP 13 minimum confirmation: marketplace ID captured
STEP 13 minimum confirmation: seller SKU mapped
STEP 13 minimum confirmation: variant status captured
STEP 13 minimum confirmation: live URL captured where available
STEP 13 minimum confirmation: latest successful sync timestamp recorded
STEP 13 output: `LIVE` status.

## 13. Listing Status Model
The product tracks granular operational status across all lifecycle phases.
Column: Status
Column: Meaning
Column: Seller Action
Listing status value: `DRAFT`
`DRAFT` meaning: Product information has been started but is not ready.
`DRAFT` seller action: Provide missing information if shown.
Listing status value: `UNDERSTANDING`
`UNDERSTANDING` meaning: Agent is interpreting product inputs.
`UNDERSTANDING` seller action: None
Listing status value: `CLASSIFYING`
`CLASSIFYING` meaning: Agent is selecting category/product type.
`CLASSIFYING` seller action: None unless ambiguous.
Listing status value: `READY_FOR_REVIEW`
`READY_FOR_REVIEW` meaning: Draft is structurally ready but requires seller confirmation.
`READY_FOR_REVIEW` seller action: Review only if requested by workflow.
Listing status value: `READY_TO_LIST`
`READY_TO_LIST` meaning: Validation passed for selected marketplace(s).
`READY_TO_LIST` seller action: None
Listing status value: `SUBMITTING`
`SUBMITTING` meaning: Listing is being sent.
`SUBMITTING` seller action: None
Listing status value: `PROCESSING`
`PROCESSING` meaning: Marketplace is processing the submission.
`PROCESSING` seller action: None
Listing status value: `LIVE`
`LIVE` meaning: Marketplace confirmed the listing is active/live.
`LIVE` seller action: None
Listing status value: `PARTIALLY_LIVE`
`PARTIALLY_LIVE` meaning: Some variants/marketplaces are live while others are not.
`PARTIALLY_LIVE` seller action: Resolve failed portions if needed.
Listing status value: `BLOCKED`
`BLOCKED` meaning: Required information/permission/compliance issue prevents progress.
`BLOCKED` seller action: Complete the displayed task.
Listing status value: `ERROR`
`ERROR` meaning: Submission/validation failed.
`ERROR` seller action: Usually none if auto-fix is possible.
`ERROR` seller action: otherwise resolve task.
Listing status value: `HUMAN_ACTION_REQUIRED`
`HUMAN_ACTION_REQUIRED` meaning: Agent cannot safely proceed without seller input/action.
`HUMAN_ACTION_REQUIRED` seller action: Answer the exact question.
`HUMAN_ACTION_REQUIRED` seller action (alternative): perform the requested marketplace action.
Listing status value: `PAUSED`
`PAUSED` meaning: Seller or system intentionally paused the listing.
`PAUSED` seller action: Resume when ready.
Listing status value: `ARCHIVED`
`ARCHIVED` meaning: Listing workflow is closed.
`ARCHIVED` seller action: None
